en.title: Lexicographically Smallest Sequence of Fewest Stable Threshold Partitions
en.description:
Array values are distinct. One operation chooses a value x present in the array, places all elements less than x first and then all elements greater than or equal to x, keeping the current relative order within each group. The goal is ascending order: first minimize the number of operations, then take the lexicographically smallest threshold sequence; if the array is already sorted, output −1.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains the resource values. 1≤n≤50, 1≤value≤10^9, all values distinct.
en.output: Output the threshold sequence separated by spaces; if no operation is needed, output only −1.
en.explanation: The answers are 2 3 4 6, 10 14 and −1. The source's second example output 14 15 belongs to a different array, and 15 is not in the actual input; this site corrects it to 10 14 according to the given input.
hints: Sort the values into b and record the original positions pos; output, in ascending order, every b[i] satisfying pos[b[i−1]]>pos[b[i]].
